decisive_items: struck by lightning directly to the right forehead while hiking
mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in right eye
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye
response.rationale: Direct lightning strike is the unifying cause of the delayed posterior subcapsular cataract and the OCT-documented maculopathy; alternatives each capture only a component finding.

rejected.why: Intraretinal cystoid changes alone do not account for the outer retinal loss, subfoveal hyporeflective space, or later cataract.
Outer retinal/photoreceptor changes are one component but miss the intraretinal cystoid changes and cataract.
Lightning-induced cataract explains the delayed lens finding but does not explain the earlier visual loss and macular OCT changes.
Traumatic maculopathy accounts for the macular findings but fails to explain the subsequent posterior subcapsular cataract from the same electrical injury.
